chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The leper (one with al-barsa'), the blind one, and the lame one are returned (i.e., the marriage contract is annulled).

key_terms.الْبَرْصَاءُ: Leper or one suffering from al-barsa' (a specific skin disease/leprosy)
key_terms.تُرَدُّ: Are returned (referring to annulment of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What physical defects invalidate a marriage contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in *al-Istibsar* identifies leprosy (al-Barṣāʾ), blindness (al-ʿamāʾ), and lameness (al-ʿarjāʾ) as specific physical defects warranting the right of *khiyār al-ʿayb* (option of defect) in Shia jurisprudence. It reflects the juristic consensus that these conditions, being visible and potentially affecting marital harmony or procreation, allow the informed spouse to annul the contract if the other was unaware. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and mutual consent in marriage contracts to prevent future discord.
